title: Until the Light Fades
subtitle: The final spark in their eyes, fading slowly.

items.text: A brilliant flash splits the darkened sky in two, and a thunderous roar scatters the shadows. All fear and unease are forgotten in an instant.
Every head turns to the place where the lightning struck to see a colossal beast standing in solemn majesty. The crowd falls silent. Then, a single young voice cries out.

items.speaker: Child
items.text: Mommy, look, it's Qiángliáng!
The child raises a lantern excitedly.

items.speaker: Child
items.text: It's just like the painting on my lantern.
The paper-crafted beast bears little resemblance to the mighty guardian towering in the distance.
Yet something in its stern, round-eyed face carries something of its righteous spirit. As the crowd shifts their gaze between the small paper lanterns and the guardian, their voices finally return.

items.speaker: Enraged Man
items.text: You're right. It's the legendary Xiǎndào Beast. Look, it has the tail of a snake and the head of a tiger, just like the illustrations.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: Has the legendary Qiángliáng come to save us? Does that mean that girl is its Zhènzǐ?

items.speaker: Woman
items.text: What are you two yapping about? Xiǎndào Beast? Zhènzǐ? Those are just fairytales. Didn't Mr. Zhōu say this was all part of a film shoot?

items.speaker: Private Investigator
items.text: Th-That's right. I told you this was all for a movie. Why don't you guys believe me?

items.speaker: Chinatown Resident
items.text: Come on, you're always full of hot air. That said, there's no way this is real. It must just be some fancy special effects. So I'll believe you this once.

items.speaker: Tourist
items.text: Wait, so all those things were fake? I almost freaked out when those ghosts came out. Their costumes and makeup were so real-looking.

items.speaker: Tourist
items.text: Man, am I glad I came to Chinatown. This parade's been insane. I gotta take more photos.
The fear that once filled their hearts gradually fades. Those who understand the truth exchange knowing smiles.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: Whoa! That's Qiángliáng, huh? Looks totally awesome.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: I heard that a descendant of the Twelve Zhènzǐ joined the Vigiles Bureau, but this is the first time I've ever seen Qiángliáng in action.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Phew, looks like they've got that actor lady under control.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Now all we need to do is grab that cursed film reel and break the barrier, and the victims will be sane again. It'll be happily ever after for everyone—
Before she can finish speaking, her optimistic prediction is ruthlessly overturned.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: What the ...? This again?!

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Wh-What's going on? Didn't they finish the job?
An anomaly even greater than the last crashes down upon them. Startled cries rise from the crowd.

items.speaker: Chinatown Resident
items.text: Look!

items.speaker: Chinatown Resident
items.text: Páifāng. Something's wrong with it.
Something is very wrong indeed. What was assumed to be a mere optical distortion is now starting to seep into tangible reality.
It is undeniably interfering with the physical world.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: I-Is that archway melting?

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: It kinda looks like a burning piece of film.
They look at each other, finding the same alarm in each other's faces.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: Wait, the barrier was created by that spooky film reel, right? Then, this means it's—

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: It's falling apart. We need to get outta here.

items.speaker: Deputy Chief Elden
items.text: Get everyone away from the edges of the barrier. The further they are from those twisting buildings, the better.

items.speaker: Private Investigator
items.text: Understood! But what the hell's going on? I thought you had the target locked down?

items.speaker: Deputy Chief Elden
items.text: We do. But clearly, this isn't over yet. Ms. Latham, anything you can do?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Yes, sir! But I'll need a few of your men.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: I can use the containment incantation they taught me at work, but I don't think it'll hold for long.

items.speaker: Deputy Chief Elden
items.text: Just do your best. In the meantime, we'll eliminate the problem at the source.
Elden's furious gaze lands on Qí Xīng.

items.speaker: Deputy Chief Elden
items.text: Alright, Qí Xīng, whatever you're doing with the reel, stop it now, or I'll make you stop it.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: I'm not doing anything.
She stands, her hat a few feet away, her body slumped against the wall behind her as she barely manages to stay upright. She forces a crooked grin.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: It's the film reel. It's reached its limit.
From her coat, she pulls out the object responsible for all this chaos.
Had Liáng not once held the film reel herself, she might not have recognized it at all.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: The Reunion of the Three Swallows? What's happening to it?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Wait, there's something else here.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: No doubt about it! Evil spirits! An insane number of them!
An-an shoves through the crowd, rushing to Qí Xīng's side. With just one glance at the film reel, her face goes pale.
Upon hearing An-an's words, Liáng's expression darkens.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: So you think so, too? We had a similar encounter at the City Hall not long ago.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Mr. Wong must've lost some of his spiritual energy to the film reel, leaving his body open to wandering evil spirits.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Since then, I've suspected that—
The uneasy speculation lodges in her throat, but An-an voices it for her.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: Of course! Aiyah, I should've realized earlier.
The ghost hunter lets out a long, frustrated sigh, then furrows her brows in thought, her expression growing increasingly grim.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: Obviously, evil spirits would be attracted to the film reel. It's like leaving a pot of honey in front of a wasp's nest.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: A living soul is a wandering spirit's favorite meal, so with the number of souls gathered in the film reel, it's like a total feast.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: All that evil spiritual energy must have the film reel bursting at the seams.
An-an scans her surroundings, alarm in her eyes. The collapse is approaching fast. It's as if reality itself is about to be swallowed whole.
Yet neither Liáng nor An-an can see a single wandering or evil spirit. A sudden realization strikes Liáng. Her gaze snaps to Qí Xīng.
But upon seeing her, her eyes widen in shock.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Ms. Qí Xīng, your hand!

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: *cough* I must admit ...
Deep, jagged cracks have spread across the entire film reel and climbed up Qí Xīng's hand and arm like sinister veins.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: The film reel isn't the only thing at its limit. I can't hold on much longer.
The vessel containing Qiángliáng strapped around Liáng's waist starts to shudder. To Qiángliáng, the malevolent energy emanating from Qí Xīng must be eradicated.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: What does that mean?
A thought flashes through Liáng's mind.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Could it be that the film reel has been out of control since the beginning?

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: That depends on how you define the beginning.
Even though Qí Xīng avoids answering, Liáng knows she's right.
Scattered pieces of the puzzle find their place, and finally, the picture begins to form a whole.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Since the moment Ms. Latham played the cursed film, people have started to suffer from mental disorders. But if you think about it, the sequence of events doesn't make sense.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: There were only five victims of the "film incident" in Hong Kong eight years ago. But this time, the number of victims was growing rapidly. That was until you got involved, Ms. Qí Xīng.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Ever since you took possession of the film reel, only a small number of specific people have been targeted. We thought you were exploiting the reel's power to carry out your vigilantism, but in truth ...

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: You were trying to control the reel by limiting its victims to those you deemed as villains.
Though disbelief still colors her voice, her words are not a question.
Elden and the others stare, caught between shock and suspicion, as they turn toward the woman they assumed was the true culprit.

items.speaker: Deputy Chief Elden
items.text: Is that true?

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: You flatter me, little vigil. I simply didn't want her legacy to become a tool of evil. That was never her intention.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: So that's why you did all this? You wanted us all at the parade because you were losing control of the reel?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: But isn't your goal to kill Ms. Noire? Was that also a setup?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: If the film reel wasn't part of your plan, then what was?
A conclusion she herself once stated resurfaces in her mind, and she realizes she made a critical error.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Ms. Qí Xīng still can't accept the way Ms. Noire ended Detective C07 III. That's her motive.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: The ending consists of two major elements: the Shèhuǒ Parade and a villain who should've been punished.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: She now sees Noire as that villain.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Noire isn't the villain, is she?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: In your perfect grand finale, the villain you intend to kill at the parade is none other than yourself.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: It's a good ending for everyone. The big bad finally gets her comeuppance.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: And who better fits the role than me?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: This is the grand finale you want to have? But why does it have to end like this?

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Because this is the way it has to be.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: When a drop of ink falls onto paper, no matter how hard you wipe, it can never be spotless again.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: People say that "Every saint has a past, and every sinner has a future." Heh, what garbage. Some mistakes can never be forgiven.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: What happened to Hé Rìjūn was an accident. You shouldn't blame yourself for her death. It wasn't your fault.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: But it was my fault. It was my stubbornness, my selfishness, that pushed my dear friend, who really, truly cared for me, toward the cliff.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: How can someone like me carry the title of C07? I don't deserve to stand in the spotlight ever again.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Heh, punishing those equally despicable pieces of scum made me feel better for a while, but it didn't last.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: That sickening feeling inside, that disgust in myself, it wouldn't stop. I looked everywhere for a way to heal it. But then I realized ...

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: ... that the biggest piece of scum was me.
Qí Xīng looks up at the sky and lets out a long breath. For the first time, her expression softens, as if she has finally released a burden, and within her eyes, something new flickers—hope.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: The answer was so simple. I can hardly believe it took me so long to see it. And now, it's time to put an end to this nauseating nightmare.
Liáng cannot understand it.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: No, you're being too harsh on yourself. Hé Rìjūn doesn't blame you. I'm certain of it.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Quit it, vigil. Look around you. Can you still claim that I'm not to blame?

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Well, I can. And let me tell you. Teresa was much stronger than you say she was.
Liáng turns to see Poitier helping Noire back into her wheelchair.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Yes, Teresa would cry often, but that made her no less determined of an artist, and before long she'd be at my door saying, "I made some edits. Take a look."

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: You know that's what she was like. Do you seriously think she gave up dreams, her life, just because of a few harsh words?

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: No! I could never have a coward like that as a partner.
Noire's face is twisted in a fury Liáng has never seen before. It sets a fire in the woman beneath her glare, making her frown in turn.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Whatever you say. Director or not, you can't tell me what to do anymore. I will have this ending.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Come on, officers, finish the job. I'd do it myself if I had the strength.
Her voice is unwavering.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: I've learned a lot these past years. If you want to save this city, you'll have to kill me. Those spirits will disappear, and everything will be back to normal.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: A perfect grand finale, isn't it? So, what are you waiting for?

items.speaker: Deputy Chief Elden
items.text: Tsk, so it's come to this, has it?
Elden swears under his breath as he reaches for the gun at his waist. Qí Xīng watches on, seemingly pleased.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Wait, sir!
Lightning shoots through Liáng's body. Her feet, once nailed to the ground, suddenly feel weightless.
She steps forward.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: There's no guarantee that things will play out like Ms. Qí Xīng said.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Please, let me try something. After all, exorcism is my and Qiángliáng's specialty.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Wait, what are you—
Before either Elden or Qí Xīng can react, the film reel is already in Liáng's grasp.

items.speaker: Deputy Chief Elden
items.text: Liáng!

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: You outta your mind or something?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Yes, there are a huge number of evil entities bound within it.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: And this is probably the most formidable opponent Qiángliáng and I have ever faced.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: But I must confront this challenge.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Not to protect the honor of my family or to mimic C07, either. But because I want to. Because it's right.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Every story has an ending, and I must act to create the best one for everyone.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Sorry, I don't have any flowery words or clever arguments, but if you're willing to help me ...

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Please, Qiángliáng, heed my call.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Ugh!

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Th-This isn't good. Is this the best I can ...

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Qiángliáng?!

items.speaker: Liang's Father
items.text: On the emperor's order, Fāngxiàngshì the Wise sought the assistance of the twelve gods of Shètí. Bestowed with their divine might, Fāngxiàngshì bound the creatures and turned their monstrous power to the service of the people. These creatures became known as the Xiǎndào Beasts, guardians of the perilous path.

items.speaker: Liang's Father
items.text: However, even formidable creatures such as these couldn't defend against all the evil spirits across the continent.

items.speaker: Liang's Father
items.text: But the people never gave up, for they knew that as long as they kept fighting ...

items.speaker: Liang's Father
items.text: ... a Xiǎndào Beast would one day come to their aid, expelling the fiends and restoring peace and prosperity.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Qiángliáng, no!
